newsitem.title: USA: Gore urges Congress to pass redevelopment programs.
newsitem.headline: Gore urges Congress to pass redevelopment programs.

text.p: Vice-President Al Gore urged Congress Friday to approve two programs that the Clinton administration believes will help revitalize America's cities.

Speaking at the annual meeting of the U.S. Conference of Mayors in San Francisco, Gore said he was concerned by Congress' refusal so far to support a second round of "empowerment zones," expanding the zones already created in a number of American cities.

Gore said an empowerment zone in Detroit and "its promises of federal tax breaks have generated vast new investment in the city and created already more than 3,800 new jobs. It's an amazing story and it's one we can replicate."
But current congressional tax bills do not include the empowerment zone proposal "and I really believe it's unjustified," he said.

"On behalf of President Clinton, I say to the House Ways and Means Committee and to the Senate Finance Committee -- I say to the entire Congress -- for the good of our country and for the good of our cities, pass this second round of empowerment zones," Gore said.
He also urged Congress to pass a proposed $2 billion "brownfields" tax credit to promote the reuse of neglected industrial sites requiring some environmental cleanup.
The brownfields tax credit would allow businesses to expense their cleanup costs and give them an incentive to revitalize urban areas, Gore said.

"This tax incentive was also part of the original balanced budget deal and here too I'm going to formally call on Congress to make sure that it is contained in the tax bill that is now moving through both houses of Congress," he said.
The administration was also pushing for a $3 billion welfare-to-work job fund, he said. The money would go directly to cities and states to enable them to move citizens from welfare to work.
"I pledge this to you ... on behalf of the president and our administration: In the final budget agreement, the mayors of America will get this money," Gore said.
Gore also announced a new multi-million dollar non-profit consortium, called the Community Marketplace Development Institute, had been launched to bring retail businesses into poor communities.
Referring to the nation's expanding economy, Gore said: "America's comeback has begun to reach America's cities."
Crime has plummeted, cities have restored fiscal integrity and urban unemployment was coming down. But, he said: "We obviously still have a long way to go."
